ready1_open_rewrite.title: Dataset open-ended question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Four vials were set up to investigate bacterial transformation. Vials 1 and 2 each contained E. coli bacteria that had been made competent and had then been mixed with a plasmid containing the gene for ampicillin (pAMP) resistance. Vials 3 and 4 both contained E. coli that had also been made competent but had not been mixed with a plasmid. Each vial of bacteria was poured onto a nutrient agar plate. Vials 1 and 3 were poured onto plates that contained the antibiotic ampicillin. Vials 2 and 4 were poured onto plates that did not contain ampicillin. The figure shows what the nutrient agar plates looked like. The shaded plates represent extensive growth, and the dots represent individual bacterial colonies. Which plate or plates have only ampicillin-resistant bacteria growing on them?

method.method_draft: Create a four-row table. From the text, mark plates 1 and 2 as receiving bacteria mixed with pAMP, and plates 3 and 4 as receiving bacteria without plasmid. Also mark plates 1 and 3 as containing ampicillin, and plates 2 and 4 as lacking ampicillin. From the image, note that plate 1 has colonies, plate 2 has extensive growth, plate 3 has no growth, and plate 4 has extensive growth. On plate 1, because ampicillin is present, any growing colonies must be ampicillin-resistant; since growth is present, it has only resistant bacteria growing. Plate 2 lacks ampicillin, so both transformed resistant and untransformed nonresistant cells could grow. Plate 3 has no bacteria growing. Plate 4 lacks plasmid and ampicillin, so growing bacteria are not selected for resistance. Therefore the only qualifying plate is plate 1.

In petri dish 1 there are multiple scattered black dots, indicating that individual bacterial colonies are growing; the inside of petri dish 2 is filled with gray shading, indicating abundant/extensive growth; the inside of petri dish 3 is blank, indicating no visible growth; the inside of petri dish 4 is also filled with gray shading, indicating abundant/extensive growth. Reasoning table: Plate 1: bacteria mixed with pAMP plasmid; the culture medium contains ampicillin; the image shows individual colonies growing. Plate 2: bacteria mixed with pAMP plasmid; the culture medium does not contain ampicillin; the image shows extensive growth. Plate 3: bacteria not mixed with plasmid; the culture medium contains ampicillin; the image shows no growth. Plate 4: bacteria not mixed with plasmid; the culture medium does not contain ampicillin; the image shows extensive growth. Reasoning: Plate 1 contains ampicillin, therefore bacteria that can grow on it must have ampicillin resistance; the image shows that Plate 1 indeed has colonies growing, so the bacteria growing on Plate 1 are all ampicillin-resistant. Plate 2 does not contain ampicillin and has no antibiotic selection, therefore transformed resistant bacteria and untransformed non-resistant bacteria both may grow, and it cannot be said that there are only resistant bacteria. Plate 3 contains ampicillin but has no growth; the question asks about petri dishes in which resistant bacteria are growing, therefore Plate 3 does not fit. Plate 4 contains no plasmid and no ampicillin, and the growing bacteria have not been selected as resistant, so it also should not be judged as having only resistant bacteria. Therefore the only one that fits is Plate 1.
